principles: Owner identity is local accidental-write coordination, never authentication or Authority evidence.
Stability must be scoped by both task identity and agent-or-role identity.
Unknown or unvalidated identity inputs fail toward isolated/degraded behavior, never toward shared privilege.
Provider-specific signals stay at adapter boundaries; generic core consumes one canonical result.
drivers: Eliminate false foreign-owner rejection when one agent crosses shell/ppid boundaries.
Preserve isolation between concurrent tasks and between implementer/reviewer roles.
Keep existing explicit override, lease, stale takeover, and active takeover semantics compatible.
Make degraded fallback visible and actionable.

options.name: A: Repository/worktree token
cons: Explicitly forbidden by the accepted workstream

options.name: B: Adapter-derived task plus agent identity with bounded token fallback
pros: Matches accepted resolution order and future-host adapter model
cons: Requires lifecycle rules for generated-token storage and cleanup

options.name: C: Retain ppid identity and improve guidance
cons: Does not fix the observed self-conflict

chosen: B: Adapter-derived task plus agent identity with bounded token fallback
rationale: Derive the canonical local session id from validated task identity plus agent/role identity at host adapters, preserving an explicit LATTICE_SESSION_ID override. When a host exposes a task boundary but no stable native id, use a bounded generated token scoped to project, provider, task boundary, and agent/role; otherwise retain derived-ppid as a warned degraded fallback. This is the only option that removes the false self-conflict without collapsing independent tasks or roles.

preMortem.scenario: Two independent tasks accidentally share an adapter boundary value.
preMortem.trigger: A wrapper supplies only repository/worktree identity or reuses one task token globally.
preMortem.consequence: One task can refresh or inherit another task owner lease.
preMortem.mitigation: Require validated task identity as an independent dimension and add same-repo/same-worktree different-task negative tests.

preMortem.scenario: Implementer and reviewer collapse to one owner identity.
preMortem.trigger: The adapter hashes thread id but omits agent/role identity.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer isolation and owner-gated mutation boundaries are weakened.
preMortem.mitigation: Require normalized agentOrRoleIdentity in the composite and test implementer, verification-intent, reviewer, and delivery separation.

preMortem.scenario: Generated tokens dirty evidence or live forever.
preMortem.trigger: Fallback storage is unregistered, not ignored, or lacks bounded ownership and cleanup.
preMortem.consequence: Material hashes drift, stale tokens accumulate, or sessions are unintentionally reused.
preMortem.mitigation: Register the path in runtime-artifact-registry, exclude it from material hashes, scope it to task+agent boundary, and define cleanup/doctor behavior.

preMortem.trigger: Raw task/session tokens are logged as nativeSessionRef or process-event fields.
preMortem.consequence: Local logs expose reusable host identifiers.
preMortem.mitigation: Hash/derive the canonical id and render only provider/source plus a redacted digest prefix; assert raw-token absence in tests.

preMortem.scenario: The fix silently changes takeover behavior.
preMortem.trigger: Lease equality or migration code rewrites foreign/stale ownership decisions along with identity resolution.
preMortem.consequence: Active foreign leases may be seized or legitimate takeover may fail.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep lease/takeover state machine untouched and run active foreign, stale takeover, force takeover, and legacy lease compatibility regressions.
